refund.title: Cancellation & Refund Policy
refund.description: How cancellations, date changes, road closures, park closures and refunds work for Northeast India trips booked with Shillong Trip.
refund.lede: Clear rules for what happens if you cancel, if we cancel, or if a road, park or permit closes. If your written quote sets different terms for a booking, the quote applies.
refund.body:
Summary

  • Cancel 30 or more days before arrival and the charge is 10% of the trip cost.
  • Closer to travel the charge rises, up to 100% inside 7 days.
  • If a landslide, flood, snow on Sela or a permit suspension closes part of your route, we reroute at no extra service charge or refund unused ground services that suppliers release.
  • Refunds reach your original payment method within 7 to 10 working days of approval.

Booking and payment

A booking is confirmed when we receive the deposit in your quote (usually 25% to 30%) and send written confirmation. The balance is due 15 days before arrival, or 30 days for peak dates: Durga Puja weeks, 1–10 December (Hornbill Festival) and 20 December–5 January.

If you cancel

Send cancellations in writing (email or WhatsApp). Charges are a percentage of the total trip cost, counted from the day we receive your message:

When you cancelCharge
30 days or more before arrival10%
29 to 15 days25%
14 to 7 days50%
6 days or less, or no-show100%

Some items follow the supplier’s own rules and can be non-refundable once booked: flights, trains, helicopter seats, Kaziranga safari bookings, festival-period stays (Hornbill, Ziro), non-refundable hotel rates and special permits. Your quote lists which items fall into this group.

Changing your dates

You can move your dates once without a change fee if you tell us 21 or more days before arrival, subject to availability and any price difference. Later changes are treated as a cancellation and a new booking.

Roads, weather, parks and permits

Hill roads close after landslides and heavy rain, the Tawang road can close after snow at Sela, national parks close for floods, and authorities sometimes suspend permits or issue advisories at short notice. These events are outside our control. When they happen:

  • We offer the best available alternative of similar value, for example an extra day in Shillong instead of Sohra, or Dirang instead of Tawang.
  • If no alternative is possible, we refund unused ground services that hotels, transporters and permit offices release, minus costs already incurred.
  • Extra costs caused by a closure, such as an extra night or a longer detour, are paid locally by the traveller.
  • We cannot refund sightseeing missed because an area was closed (for example Bum La after snowfall, a safari range shut for the day, or Dawki boating suspended in the monsoon).

If we cancel

If we cancel for a reason within our control, you get a full refund. If we cancel because travel is unsafe or prohibited, we refund what suppliers return to us, or hold it as credit for a later trip if you prefer.

Unused services

Services not used during the trip are not refundable. If a traveller must leave early for health reasons, we help with transport and medical support, but unused services are not refunded. We recommend travel insurance covering cancellation and medical evacuation.

How refunds are paid

Approved refunds go to the original payment method within 7 to 10 working days. Bank or gateway charges (typically 2% to 3%) and non-refundable supplier costs are deducted.

terms.title: Terms & Conditions
terms.description: Terms and conditions for booking Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal and Northeast India trips: prices, payments, permits, health, conduct, liability and jurisdiction.
terms.lede: The agreement between you and us when you book. Please read it before paying a deposit.
terms.body:
Who we are

This website is operated by @@LEGAL@@, registered with the state tourism department (registration @@REG@@), GSTIN @@GSTIN@@. Contact: @@EMAIL@@ · @@PHONE@@ · @@STREET@@, @@LOC@@, @@REGION@@, @@PIN@@.

Quotes and prices

Prices on this site are indicative starting prices per person, twin sharing, with standard hotels and a private vehicle. Your written quote gives the final price for your dates, hotels, vehicle and group size. Quotes are valid for 7 days or until the hotels in them sell out. Applicable taxes, including GST, are shown in the quote.

Booking and payment

A booking is confirmed on receipt of the deposit and our written confirmation. Payment terms and cancellation charges are in our Cancellation & Refund Policy. Pay only to the bank account or payment link in your written quote; we never ask for payment to a personal account over a phone call.

What is included

Your quote lists exactly what is and is not included. Typically included: hotels with the meals stated, a private vehicle with driver for the routes in the itinerary, permits we arrange and driver allowances. Typically not included: flights, trains, entry and camera fees, safari fees unless stated, lunches and personal expenses.

Permits and documents

Inner Line Permits (Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, Manipur), Protected Area Permits and special passes such as Bum La are issued by government offices, not by us. We apply on your behalf with the documents you send. Carry original photo ID (and passports and visas for foreign nationals) throughout the trip. If a permit is refused or suspended, our closure terms apply.

Health and altitude

Arunachal routes reach about 4,200 m at Sela Pass and higher at Bum La. You are responsible for being fit to travel and for consulting a doctor, particularly with heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions, during pregnancy or with infants. Treks such as Nongriat involve thousands of steps. Tell us about medical conditions so we can adjust the plan.

Vehicles and drivers

Local rules and taxi associations govern tourist vehicles in several towns (for example Sohra, Dawki and Tawang). Vehicles run on the routes in your itinerary; point-to-point changes, night driving and routes outside the plan may not be allowed or may cost extra. Air-conditioning is generally not used on hill roads.

Your conduct

Follow local laws and customs: villages such as Mawlynnong and sacred forests such as Mawphlang have their own rules, monasteries and satras expect modest dress, and photography is not allowed near army installations. We may end services without refund if a traveller behaves dangerously or illegally.

Our responsibility

We choose hotels, transporters and guides with care, but they are independent suppliers. We are not liable for loss, injury, delay or extra cost caused by events outside our control, including weather, landslides, floods, road or park closures, strikes, government action or acts of the traveller. Our total liability for any claim is limited to the amount paid to us for the affected services.

Travel insurance

We strongly recommend travel insurance covering cancellation, medical treatment and evacuation. It is not included unless your quote says so.

Website content

We keep information accurate, but permits, fares, timings and road status change. See our disclaimer. Photos are credited to their Wikimedia Commons authors; see photo credits.

Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of India. Disputes are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts at Shillong, Meghalaya.

Grievance officer

@@GNAME@@, Grievance Officer can be reached at @@GEMAIL@@ · @@GPHONE@@. We acknowledge complaints within 48 hours and aim to resolve them within 30 days.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: What personal data Shillong Trip collects when you enquire or book, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it and your rights under Indian law.
privacy.lede: We collect only what we need to plan and run your trip. This policy follows India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
privacy.body:
What we collect

  • Enquiry details: name, phone or WhatsApp number, email, travel month, travellers, preferences and messages.
  • Booking details: ID documents and photos needed for permits, dietary or medical notes you choose to share, and payment records.
  • How you found us: the page you enquired from and campaign tags in the link you followed, stored in your browser and sent with your enquiry.
  • Analytics, only with consent: anonymous usage data such as pages viewed and device type.

Why we use it

  • To reply to your enquiry and prepare a quote.
  • To book hotels, vehicles, safaris and permits.
  • To contact you about your booking, including road or permit changes.
  • To understand which pages help travellers so we can improve the site.
  • To meet legal, tax and accounting obligations.

We do not sell your data or use it for third-party advertising.

Consent

Sending an enquiry means you consent to us using your details to respond. You can withdraw consent any time by writing to us; this does not affect processing already done or records the law requires us to keep.

Who we share it with

  • Hotels, transport operators, safari offices and guides on your trip, only what they need.
  • Government offices that issue permits (names, ID details and photos).
  • Service providers that help us operate, such as email and spreadsheet tools, WhatsApp when you choose to message us, and analytics if you consent. Some may store data outside India.
  • Authorities where required by law.

How long we keep it

Enquiries that do not become bookings are deleted within 24 months. Booking and payment records are kept as long as tax law requires (currently up to 8 years). Permit documents are deleted after your trip unless the law requires otherwise.

Your rights

You can ask to access, correct, update or erase your personal data, withdraw consent and nominate someone to act for you. Write to @@EMAIL@@; we reply within 30 days.

Security

We limit access to people who need it, use two-step sign-in on our accounts, and never ask for card numbers or passwords over WhatsApp or email.

Children

We collect children’s details only from a parent or guardian, and only to book travel and permits.

Cookies

See our Cookie Policy. Change your choice any time with “Cookie settings” in the footer.

Grievance officer

@@GNAME@@, Grievance Officer can be reached at @@GEMAIL@@ · @@GPHONE@@. We acknowledge complaints within 48 hours and aim to resolve them within 30 days.

If you are not satisfied with our response, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.description: Which cookies and browser storage Shillong Trip uses, why, and how to accept, reject or change your choice.
cookies.lede: A short list of what this site stores in your browser. Essential items are always on; analytics only runs if you say yes.
cookies.body:
Essential storage

Kept in your browser’s local storage and not sent to us:

NamePurposeKept for

st_consentYour cookie choice12 months

Analytics (optional)

If you accept, we may load Google Analytics 4, which sets cookies such as _ga and _ga_* for up to 13 months to count visits. If you reject, no analytics script loads.

Third-party services

Fonts load from Google Fonts, which receives your IP address to deliver them. Links to WhatsApp, maps and social networks take you to those services, whose own policies apply.

Changing your choice

Use “Cookie settings” in the footer, or clear this site’s data in your browser. Rejecting analytics does not affect how the site works.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.description: Limits of the travel information on Shillong Trip: permits, road status, park seasons, prices, altitude advice, photos and external links.
disclaimer.lede: We check facts carefully, but the Northeast changes quickly. Please read this before relying on anything on the site.
disclaimer.body:
Travel information

Permit rules, road status, park seasons, fares and timings change often, sometimes overnight after landslides, floods or official orders. Information here reflects what we found when it was last checked. Confirm the current position with us or the relevant authority before you travel.

Prices

Prices are indicative starting prices and are not an offer. Your written quote is the only binding price.

Health

Advice on altitude, treks and fitness is general information, not medical advice. Consult a doctor before travelling.

Not a government website

This is a private tour operator’s website. We are not affiliated with any state government, tourism department, forest department or the Indian Army. Permits are issued by the relevant government offices.

Photos

Photos are from Wikimedia Commons contributors, used under their licences and credited on each photo and on our photo credits page. They may not show conditions on your dates.

External links

Links to other websites are for convenience; we are not responsible for their content.

home_faqs.q: How many days do I need for Meghalaya?
home_faqs.a: Four to five nights covers Shillong, Sohra (Cherrapunji), Dawki and Mawlynnong at a comfortable pace. Add a night in Sohra or Nongriat if you want the Double Decker root bridge trek, and two nights for Kaziranga if you are combining Assam. A weekend is enough for Shillong alone.

home_faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Shillong and Meghalaya?
home_faqs.a: October to April is the most reliable: dry trails, clear water at Dawki from about November, and cool, sunny days. June to September is monsoon, when waterfalls are at their fullest but treks get slippery and roads can close after landslides. Kaziranga is open roughly November to April.

Most travellers fly or take a train to Guwahati, then drive about 100 km (around 3 hours) to Shillong on a good four-lane highway. Shillong’s own airport at Umroi has very few flights, and there is no railway line into the city, so plan around Guwahati.

home_faqs.q: Do I need a permit for the Northeast?
home_faqs.a: Meghalaya and Assam need no permit for Indian citizens. Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur require an Inner Line Permit (ILP) for Indians, usually issued online. Foreign nationals follow separate Protected Area rules in some states. Our permit checker lists the current rule for each state.

home_faqs.q: When is Kaziranga National Park open?
home_faqs.a: Kaziranga usually opens in phases from October or November and closes around the end of April or May, before the monsoon floods the grasslands. Jeep safaris run in the morning and afternoon, and elephant safaris early in the morning in some ranges. Dates change each year, so check before booking.

home_faqs.q: Can I combine Shillong, Kaziranga and Tawang in one trip?
home_faqs.a: Yes, but give it at least 9 to 10 nights. Tawang is roughly two days’ drive from Guwahati with a night in Dirang or Bomdila on the way, so it adds four or five nights on its own. Meghalaya and Kaziranga together fit comfortably into 6 or 7 nights.

home_faqs.q: Is the Northeast safe for tourists?
home_faqs.a: Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal, Nagaland, Mizoram and Tripura see large numbers of tourists every year without trouble. Road safety on mountain routes and monsoon landslides are the main practical risks. Some parts of Manipur have had travel advisories in recent years, so we check current guidance before planning any Manipur trip.

home_faqs.q: How much does a Meghalaya trip cost?
home_faqs.a: A 4-night Meghalaya trip with standard hotels, breakfast and a private car typically starts around ₹14,000 to ₹20,000 per person for two people sharing. Kaziranga safaris, premium resorts, peak dates such as Durga Puja and Christmas, and solo travel add to the cost. Ask us for an exact quote for your dates.

home_faqs.q: Is Dawki’s river really that clear?
home_faqs.a: Yes, in the dry months. The Umngot at Dawki and Shnongpdeng is usually glass-clear from about November to April, when boats appear to float on air. From June to September, monsoon rain turns it muddy and boating can be suspended, so time your visit for the dry season if clear water is the goal.

more_faqs.q: Which airport should I fly into?
more_faqs.a: Guwahati’s Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (GAU) is the main gateway for Meghalaya, Kaziranga and western Arunachal, with direct flights from most Indian metros. For upper Assam and eastern Arunachal, Dibrugarh or Jorhat can save a long drive. For Nagaland, fly to Dimapur.

more_faqs.q: What vehicle will we travel in?
more_faqs.a: Couples usually travel in a sedan such as a Dzire on the Guwahati–Shillong–Sohra circuit. For Arunachal, Kaziranga and larger groups we use SUVs such as the Innova, Xylo or Scorpio, and tempo travellers for groups of eight or more. Your quote names the vehicle type.

more_faqs.q: Is there mobile network and internet?
more_faqs.a: Shillong, Guwahati, Sohra, Tezpur and Tawang town have 4G on major networks. Coverage drops in Nongriat, Mawlynnong’s surroundings, parts of the Tawang road, Mechuka and inside national parks. Carry offline maps and tell family you may be out of touch for a day on treks.

more_faqs.q: Are ATMs and UPI widely accepted?
more_faqs.a: UPI works in most shops and hotels in Shillong, Guwahati and Tawang town. Carry cash for village homestays, parking, boat rides at Dawki, root-bridge trail fees and small eateries, where network or card machines may not work. ATMs in remote towns can run dry at weekends.

Yes, with a Protected Area Permit arranged through a registered tour operator; rules on group size and fees have changed over recent years, so we confirm the current position when you enquire. Some border points, including Bum La, remain closed to foreign nationals.

more_faqs.q: Do you arrange Kaziranga safari bookings?
more_faqs.a: Yes. We book jeep safaris through the official system and can request elephant safari slots where they run, subject to availability. Morning slots in the Central range fill first in peak months, so book at least two to three weeks ahead between December and March.

more_faqs.q: What happens if a road closes?
more_faqs.a: Landslides in the monsoon and snow on Sela in winter can close roads for hours or days. We watch conditions daily and reroute where possible. If part of a trip cannot run, our cancellation and refund policy explains what is refunded and what extra costs apply.

more_faqs.q: Can you plan group and corporate trips?
more_faqs.a: Yes. We plan school groups, family reunions and company offsites of 10 to 60 people, mostly around Guwahati, Shillong and Kaziranga, with tempo travellers or small coaches, conference-friendly hotels and a single point of contact for the group.

more_faqs.q: Is Meghalaya good for a trip with young children?
more_faqs.a: Yes, with the right choices. Shillong, Elephant Falls, Mawsmai Cave, Mawlynnong and a Dawki boat ride all suit children. Skip the full Nongriat trek with under-8s and avoid long monsoon drives. We plan shorter driving days and hotels with space for families.

about_faqs.q: Which parts of the Northeast do you cover?
about_faqs.a: Meghalaya (Shillong, Sohra, Dawki, the Jaintia and Garo hills), Assam (Guwahati, Kaziranga, Manas, Majuli, upper Assam tea country), Arunachal Pradesh (Tawang, Dirang, Ziro, Mechuka, Namdapha) and Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. Most trips combine two or three of these.

about_faqs.q: Can you change one of your packages?
about_faqs.a: Yes. Almost every trip we run is adjusted before booking: change the pace, swap a place, add a Kaziranga safari or a root-bridge trek, or upgrade hotels. Tell us what to change and we send a revised day-by-day plan and a new price.

about_faqs.q: Do you arrange ILPs and safari bookings?
about_faqs.a: Yes. We handle Inner Line Permits for Arunachal, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur, request Bum La passes in Tawang for Indian nationals, and book Kaziranga jeep safaris through the official system. You send clear ID copies; we file and keep you updated.

about_faqs.q: What happens if a road or park closes during my trip?
about_faqs.a: We tell you as soon as we know and offer the best alternative, such as an extra day in Shillong, a different safari range or Dirang instead of Tawang. If nothing similar is possible, we refund unused ground services suppliers release, as set out in our refund policy.

A deposit, usually 25% to 30%, confirms the booking, and the balance is due about 15 days before arrival (30 days for peak dates such as Durga Puja, Hornbill and New Year). Pay only to the account or payment link in your written quote.

about_faqs.q: Do you book flights and trains?
about_faqs.a: We focus on ground arrangements: hotels, vehicles, permits, safaris and guides. We suggest the best flights into Guwahati, Dibrugarh or Dimapur for your dates and time pickups around them, but we recommend you book tickets directly.

about_faqs.q: Do you plan trips for foreign travellers?
about_faqs.a: Yes. We plan routes that work with permit rules for non-Indian passports, arrange Protected Area Permits where needed through registered channels, and flag places such as Bum La that remain closed to foreign nationals.

about_faqs.q: Is the Northeast good for families and older travellers?
about_faqs.a: Yes, with sensible pacing. We keep driving days short, avoid stacking long treks, pick hotels with lifts or ground-floor rooms where needed, and add rest days before high-altitude stretches such as Sela and Tawang.

Usually within one working day with a first plan and price. In peak weeks (October, December and the Hornbill period) it can take a little longer, and WhatsApp is the fastest way to reach us. We never pressure anyone to book on the spot.

promises: Real drive times, not brochure ones. Guwahati to Shillong is three hours; Guwahati to Tawang is two days, and we say so.
Dawki in the dry months, falls in the wet ones, Sela with a buffer day. We time trips for what you came to see.
Hotels, vehicle, permits, safari slots and what’s not included, all on paper before you pay.
Drivers from the hills, village homestays in Nongriat, Mawlynnong and Ziro, and guides who grew up there.
Official safari slots only, no pushing for closer sightings, and parks visited in season.
Our photos come from Wikimedia Commons photographers, credited by name on every image.
